Due to the expansionary fiscal policy adopted by the Government of India in the 1980s—such as large budget deficits year after year, excessive government borrowing, and an increase in dissaving—income increased; consequently, demand for consumer goods also increased. This is clear from the fact that in the Seventh Five-Year Plan, the per capita income growth rate was 3.7% per year, higher than earlier plans. Further, while the growth rate of consumer goods industries was about 5–6% and 6.7% per year during 1974– 79 and 1980–85 respectively, it was about 7–8% per year during 1985–90. Hence, the reason is incorrect.

questions.q: The average annual growth in non-development expenditure in the Seventh Five-Year Plan is -
questions.explanation: Non-development expenditure increased from Rs. 30,564 crore in 1985–86 to Rs. 70,626 crore in 1990–91. Thus, during this period, the annual growth in non-development expenditure was 26.21 percent. Rapid increases under heads such as interest payments, security, fiscal services, administrative services, pensions, and subsidies were the factors responsible for the sharp rise in non-development expenditure.

questions.q: Which of the following Five-Year Plans was focused on human resource development?

options.D: More than one of the above
options.E: None of the above

questions.explanation: The Eighth Five-Year Plan was focused on human resource development. Note that the Eighth Five-Year Plan was from 1992 to 1997. The Eighth Five-Year Plan is not mentioned in the given options; hence option (e) is correct.

questions.q: The Eighth Five-Year Plan gives priority to-
questions.explanation: The Eighth Five-Year Plan (1992–97) was based on the John W. Miller model, adopted in the context of a liberalised economy. In this plan, human resource development was the basic objective, and it aimed at generating adequate employment to achieve near full employment by the end of the century.

questions.q: What is the duration of India's Eighth Five- Year Plan?
questions.explanation: The Eighth Five-Year Plan (1992–97) was based on the John W. Miller model, adopted in the context of a liberalised economy. In this plan, human resource development was the basic objective, and it aimed at generating adequate employment to achieve near full employment by the end of the century.

questions.q: The target for increasing GDP under the Eighth Plan was set at-
questions.explanation: In the Eighth Plan, the target for the growth rate of Gross Domestic Product (GDP) was fixed at 5.6 percent. This was lower than the actual growth achieved during the plan period (6.8 percent) and slightly lower than the actual growth rate of 6 percent achieved in the Seventh Plan. The actual growth achieved in the Eighth Plan was 6.8 percent.

questions.q: The 9th Five Year Plan of India is the period of-
questions.explanation: The duration of the Ninth Five-Year Plan was from 1 April 1997 to 31 March 2002.

questions.q: What is the duration of the 10th Five-Year Plan?
questions.explanation: The duration of the Tenth Five-Year Plan was from 2002 to 2007.

questions.q: The objective of the Eleventh Five-Year Plan is :
questions.explanation: The broad objective of the Eleventh Five-Year Plan (1 April 2007 to 31 March 2012) was to achieve inclusive growth. In the National Development Council (NDC) meeting held in December 2007, the draft of the Eleventh Five-Year Plan was approved, while its Approach Paper was approved in the NDC meeting held in December 2006. The theme of the Eleventh Five-Year Plan was “Towards Faster and More Inclusive Growth”.

questions.q: During Twelfth Five-Year Plan, which one of the following average annual growth rate targets was envisaged for agriculture and allied sector?

options.E: None of the above/More than one of the above

questions.explanation: In the Twelfth Five-Year Plan (2012–17), a target of 8 percent real GDP growth rate was set. Among other things, the Twelfth Plan aimed to achieve a 4 percent growth rate for agriculture and allied sectors. The target of the Twelfth Five- Year Plan was “Faster, Sustainable and More Inclusive Growth”.

questions.q: The 'Rolling Plan' concept in National Planning was introduced by :
questions.explanation: Gunnar Myrdal, in his book ‘Indian Economic Planning in its Broader Setting’, recommended the Rolling Plan for developing countries. This concept was implemented in 1978–79 by the coalition government formed under the leadership of the Janata Party.

questions.q: Consider the following about the 'Rolling Plan' : I. A plan for the current year which includes the annual budget II. A plan for a fixed number of years, say 3, 4 or 5 III. It is revised every year as per the requirements of the economy IV. A perspective plan for 10, 15 or 20 years Which of the above are correct?
questions.explanation: A ‘Rolling Plan’ is a flexible planning approach. Under it, three plans are prepared—short-term (for one year), mediumterm (for 3–5 years) and long-term (for 10–20 years). Necessary modifications are made every year as per requirements. Thus, it is a flexible plan that moves forward by adjusting itself according to circumstances.

questions.q: Who is the head of the District Planning and Development Council?

options.A: The Finance Minister of the State

questions.explanation: The head of the District Planning and Development Council is the District Planning Officer.

questions.q: The Foreign Exchange Reserves (FER) of RBI include which of the following? 1. Foreign Currency Assets (FCA) 2. Gold 3. Special Drawing Rights (SDR) 4. Reserve Tranche Position Select the correct answer using the codes given below.
questions.explanation: The Reserve Bank of India’s foreign exchange reserves refer to reserve assets held by the RBI. These include foreign currency assets (such as bonds, Treasury bills and other government securities), along with gold, Special Drawing Rights (SDR), and the reserve position in the IMF. The following are included— • Foreign Currency Assets (FCA) • Gold • Special Drawing Rights (SDR) • Reserve position in the IMF

questions.q: Consider the following statements regarding insolvency and bankruptcy : 1. Bankruptcy refers to a financial state in which an individual or entity is unable to pay off their debts as they become due. 2. Insolvency refers to a legal process, where the assets of the debtor are liquidated or reorganized for the benefit of creditors. 3. Bankruptcy is a state whereas insolvency is the conclusion. 4. The Insolvency and Bankruptcy Board of India (IBBI) is the regulatory body responsible for overseeing insolvency and bankruptcy proceedings. Which of the above statements is/are correct?
questions.explanation: Insolvency means the financial condition in which a person or an institution is unable to pay its debts when they become due. Bankruptcy refers to a legal process in which the debtor’s assets are liquidated or reorganized for the benefit of creditors. Insolvency denotes a stage/condition, whereas bankruptcy is the conclusion. The Insolvency and Bankruptcy Board of India (IBBI) is the regulatory body responsible for overseeing insolvency and bankruptcy proceedings.

questions.q: Which of the following factors could potentially contribute to stagflation in the Indian economy? 1. High inflationary pressures due to increased Government spending 2. Decline in industrial production and sluggish economic growth 3. Decrease in aggregate demand and consumer spending 4. Appreciation of the domestic currency leading to a reduction in export competitiveness Select the correct answer using the codes given below.
questions.explanation: Inflation is commonly called rising prices. When, during a period, the prices of goods and services increase and people have to pay a higher price to buy the same quantity of goods and services as before, it is called inflation. In the Indian economy, the following factors can potentially contribute to stagflation—  Decline in industrial production and slowdown in economic growth.  Reduced export competitiveness due to appreciation of the domestic currency.  Decrease in aggregate demand and consumer spending.  High inflationary pressure due to an increase in government spending, etc.

questions.q: Lowering the Cash Reserve Ratio, it will have the following impact on the economy: I. Banks will have higher liquidity leverage. II. The economy may see increased investment. III. Supply of currency in the economy may broaden. IV. Real investment rate may decline. Select the correct code :

options.E: None of the above / More than one of the above

questions.explanation: Reducing the Cash Reserve Ratio (CRR) increases liquidity with banks, which can lead to a fall in interest rates, an increase in lending and investment, and an increase in money supply in the economy. Hence, statements I, II and III are true.

questions.q: In August 2019, how much principal (in crores) did the Ministry of Finance, Government of India announce to infuse to improve the liquidity and lending arrangements of public sector banks?

options.E: None of the above

questions.explanation: In August 2019, the Ministry of Finance, Government of India, announced a capital infusion of ₹70,000 crore to improve liquidity and lending in public sector banks.

questions.q: Before the launch of Kisan Rin Portal (KRP), farmers used to submit manual claims under the Interest Subvention and Prompt Repayment Incentive schemes to which of the following institutions?

options.A: Ministry of Agriculture and Farmers Welfare and NABARD
options.B: Reserve Bank of India and NABARD
options.C: National Payments Corporation of India and Reserve Bank of India
options.D: More than one of the above

questions.explanation: To provide farmers with affordable short-term crop loans, the Government of India runs the Interest Subvention Scheme (ISS) and an additional scheme for the Prompt Repayment Incentive (PRI). For transparent and faster settlement of claims, the Kisan Rin Portal (KRP) was launched in 2023. Before the launch of KRP, manual claims of interest subvention (IS) and prompt repayment incentive (PRI) were sent to the Reserve Bank of India (RBI) and NABARD. It is noteworthy that technically, farmers themselves did not directly send these claims to RBI or NABARD; rather, based on the loans given to farmers, banks sent these claims to RBI and NABARD. Therefore, the statement in the question that “farmers… submitted manual claims” is not technically correct.

questions.q: Which of the following investors or agencies can purchase Government of India securities? I. The Reserve Bank of India II. Individuals III. Financial Institution Select the correct answer using the code given below.

options.E: None of the above/More than one of the above

questions.explanation: The Reserve Bank of India, individuals, and financial institutions—all three—can buy Government of India securities. Government securities are mandatorily tradable financial instruments issued by the Central and State Governments, which acknowledge the Government’s liability for borrowing.

questions.q: How many times does Reserve Bank of India reviews the Monetary Policy in a financial year?

options.E: None of the above/More than one of the above

questions.explanation: A bimonthly monetary policy is announced by the Monetary Policy Committee (MPC) of the Reserve Bank of India (RBI), which takes place 6 times in a financial year. However, during the COVID-19 pandemic, irregularity was recorded in the bi-monthly cycle. At present, the bi-monthly monetary policy cycle has again been fixed. Therefore, option (e) is the correct answer.

questions.q: According to the Reserve Bank of India (RBI), what is the forecast for headline inflation in Financial Year 2025 ?
questions.explanation: The Reserve Bank of India had estimated that inflation would decline to 4.5% and 4.1% in FY 2025 and FY 2026 respectively. According to the Monetary Policy Report issued by the RBI in April 2025, CPI inflation for FY 2025–26 was estimated to be 4%.

questions.q: The Reserve Bank of India is using which of the following inflation indices as the anchor for 'Inflation Targeting'?

options.E: None of the above/More than one of the above

questions.explanation: The Reserve Bank of India uses CPI–Combined as the anchor for the inflation target. The following types of CPI are: (i) CPI for Industrial Workers (ii) CPI for Agricultural Labourers (iii) CPI for Rural Labourers (iv) CPI (Rural/Urban/Combined)

questions.q: As per the new methodology, the lending rate is calculated by the banks based on

options.E: None of the above/More than one of the above

questions.explanation: According to the new methodology, a bank’s lending rate is calculated on the basis of the marginal cost of funds. Marginal cost is the cost that arises only when additional units are produced beyond the normal level of production.

questions.q: The deregulation of interest rates of banks is based on the recommendation of ……….
questions.explanation: The Narasimhan Committee (1991) identified the decline in interest income as a major reason for the falling profitability of public sector banks in India. The reduction in interest income was mainly because a large part of total deposits had to be maintained at relatively low interest rates in the form of the Statutory Liquidity Ratio (SLR) and Cash Reserve Ratio (CRR). In addition, under social banking, a large share of deposits (about 40% of total deposits) had to be lent to the priority sector at low interest rates. Only about 30% of total deposits could be lent at market interest rates. In this context, the Narasimhan Committee recommended reducing SLR to 25% and bringing down CRR to around the 3% to 5% level. It also recommended giving banks the freedom to fix the minimum lending rate. The Government accepted the above recommendations of the Committee.

questions.q: To what extent did the Narasimhan Committee suggest reducing the Statutory Liquidity Ratio?
questions.explanation: In 1991, the recommendations of the Narasimhan Committee were submitted. The committee recommended a reduction in the Statutory Liquidity Ratio (SLR), suggesting that the SLR should be reduced in a phased manner over the next five years from 38.5 percent to 25 percent. In January 2007, the minimum limit of 25 percent for SLR was abolished, while the upper limit (40 percent) was retained. This means that SLR can now be between 0 and 40 percent. As of December 2025, SLR stands at 18 percent.

questions.q: R.N. Malhotra Committee is related to-
questions.explanation: The Malhotra Committee was constituted in April 1993, and its report was submitted in January 1994. As per the major recommendations of this report, the Insurance Regulatory and Development Authority Act, 1999 was enacted. The report recommended the establishment of an independent regulatory authority for the insurance sector. In April 2000, IRDA was incorporated as a statutory body. The main objectives of IRDA are to protect the interests of policyholders, ensure orderly regulation and promotion of the insurance industry, and deal with related and incidental matters.

questions.q: Bhandari Committee is related to :

options.E: None of the above/More than one of the above

questions.explanation: The Bhandari Committee (1994) was constituted for the restructuring of Regional Rural Banks (RRBs).

questions.q: The base year for All-India Wholesale Price Index (WPI) has been changed by the Government of India from 2004-05 to :

options.E: None of the above/More than one of the above

questions.explanation: In May 2017, the base year of the All-India Wholesale Price Index was revised. For measuring the WPI, the base year was changed from 2004-05 to 2011-12. Earlier, 1952-53, 1961-62, 1970-71, 1981-82, 1993-94, and 2004-05 were WPI base years. With base year 2011-12, it became the 7th WPI series.

questions.q: Consider the following Consumer Price Index : I. Consumer Price Index for Industrial Workers. II. Consumer Price Index for Agricultural Labourers. III. Consumer Price Index for Rural Workers. IV. Consumer Price Index for Urban Non-Manual Employees. In the given indices, which is/are compiled by Central Statistics Office (CSO)?
questions.explanation: The Consumer Price Index for Industrial Workers, the Consumer Price Index for Agricultural Labourers, and the Consumer Price Index for Rural Labourers are compiled by the Labour Bureau working under the Ministry of Labour and Employment, Government of India, whereas the Consumer Price Index for Urban Non-Manual Employees (CPI-UNME) used to be compiled by CSO (now under NSO) but it stopped being issued from 2008. At present, CPI-C (Combined) is being issued by the NSO.

questions.q: Financial sector reforms in India consist of :

options.A: Lowering down of CRR and SLR
options.B: Entry of private firms in the insurance sector

questions.explanation: All three mentioned above are included in financial sector reforms in India. Overall economic reforms covered many sectors. These sectors include removal of the industrial licensing system, removal of restrictions on foreign investment, reduction in import duties and gradual withdrawal of quantitative restrictions, determination of exchange rate by market forces, reforms in the financial sector, liberalisation of the capital market, private sector investment in the public sector, privatisation, reduction in excise duty, reduction in income and corporate taxes, etc.

questions.q: If the Cash Reserve Ratio is lowered by the RBI, its impact on credit creation will be :
questions.explanation: If the Reserve Bank of India reduces the Cash Reserve Ratio (CRR), the amount of credit creation by commercial banks increases.

questions.q: Which of the following is a function of the Central Bank ?
questions.explanation: The Reserve Bank of India (India’s central bank) performs the following responsibilities: → Management of monetary policy (repo rate, CRR, SLR, bank rate, etc.) → Issuer of currency → Banker to the government and manager of public debt → Banker to banks → Regulator of the banking system → Foreign exchange management, etc.

questions.q: Consider the following statements : 1. Bank Rate is the rate of interest which RBI charges its clients on their short-term borrowing. 2. Repo Rate is the rate of interest which RBI charges its clients on their long-term borrowing. Which of the statements given above is / are incorrect?
questions.explanation: According to the RBI Act, the bank rate is the rate at which the Reserve Bank rediscounts the bills of commercial banks. In practical terms, the interest rate at which commercial banks obtain long-term loans from the RBI is called the “bank rate.” The bank rate is an important part of the RBI’s monetary policy. On the other hand, at the repo rate, the RBI provides short-term loans to commercial banks. Therefore, both statements 1 and 2 are wrong.

questions.q: In Indian currency, the one rupee note is issued under the signature of :

options.A: Governor of the Reserve Bank of India
options.C: Finance Secretary, Ministry of Finance, Govt. of India

questions.explanation: The Reserve Bank of India issues currency notes of various denominations in India, except one-rupee notes. One-rupee notes are issued by the Government of India, and they carry the signature of the Secretary, Ministry of Finance.

questions.q: Which of the following payment instrument introduced by banks is known as plastic currency?
questions.explanation: Considering the changing nature of the developing economy, banking instruments are also changing. To make transactions convenient, banks started issuing credit cards to their customers. Through a credit card, a customer can pay for the purchase of goods, and an amount equal to the purchase value is transferred from the customer’s bank account to the concerned party. Credit card, debit card and cash card are collectively known as “plastic currency.”

questions.q: On October 8, 1991, the Reserve Bank of India increased the bank rate from 11% to -
questions.explanation: For that period, option (b) was the correct answer. In the monetary policy statement issued in December 2025, Bank Rate—5.50%, MSF Rate—5.50%, Repo Rate—5.25%, Standing Deposit Facility (SDF) Rate—5.00%, Reverse Repo Rate—3.35%, Cash Reserve Ratio (CRR)—3.0%, and Statutory Liquidity Ratio (SLR)—18%.

questions.q: The current rate of cash reserve ratio declared by the Reserve Bank of India is-
questions.explanation: For that period, option (b) was the correct answer. In the monetary policy statement issued in December 2025, Bank Rate—5.50%, MSF Rate—5.50%, Repo Rate—5.25%, Standing Deposit Facility (SDF) Rate—5.00%, Reverse Repo Rate—3.35%, Cash Reserve Ratio (CRR)—3.0%, and Statutory Liquidity Ratio (SLR)—18%.

questions.q: Which of the following is not directly important for economic development?
questions.explanation: Money is used as a medium of exchange, which helps in the smooth functioning of economic activities. That is, unlike price stability, the savings rate and the utilisation of resources, it contributes to economic development not directly but indirectly.

questions.q: Life Insurance Corporation is an example of-
questions.explanation: Life Insurance Corporation of India (LIC) mobilises public savings and invests them in industrial securities and government securities, or in a mix of both. Thus, LIC is an example of an investment bank. On the basis of insurance, LIC collects huge amounts of money from the public, invests them in other sectors of the economy and, through such largescale investment, earns large returns.

questions.q: When was the Life Insurance Corporation of India established?
questions.explanation: Under the LIC Act, 1956, passed by the Indian Parliament, the Life Insurance Corporation of India (LIC) was established on 1 September 1956.

questions.q: Indian currency is printed on-
questions.explanation: Among the given options, Indian currency is printed at the Currency Note Press, Nashik (Maharashtra). The currencynote printing and allied units in India are as follows- 1. Currency Note Press, Nashik 2. Bank Note Press, Dewas 3. Security Printing Press, Hyderabad 4. Security Paper Mill, Narmadapuram 5. India Security Press, Nashik The minting (coin) units are as follows- 1. Mumbai 2. Kolkata 3. Hyderabad 4. Noida

questions.q: In general, the main objective of monetary policy is-
questions.explanation: Monetary policy refers to a control policy through which the central bank controls the supply of money in order to achieve the objectives of overall economic policy. However, in a developing country like India, through monetary policy the central bank, on the one hand, regulates the volume of credit (control of money supply) and, on the other hand, also meets the monetary and credit requirements generated by development programmes.

questions.q: The capital adequacy standard for banks regulated by the Government of India is-
questions.explanation: The Basel Committee, constituted by the Bank for International Settlements, first presented the concept of capital adequacy norms in 1988. Capital adequacy means such capital which a bank should keep with it up to a specified level for creating business/commercial assets. For example, if the capital adequacy ratio is fixed at 8 percent, it means that for every Rs. 100 of business assets, the bank must mandatorily keep Rs. 8 as capital with it. In line with the Basel Committee’s recommendations, India started implementing capital adequacy norms in all banks from 1992-93. Before 31 March 2000, the capital adequacy norm was 8 percent. Under Basel III norms, it has been decided to increase the capital adequacy ratio to 9 percent from 2019.

questions.q: Hard currency means the currency which-
questions.explanation: Hard currency refers to the currencies belongs to developed countries. They are called hard currencies because, compared to their supply, their demand is higher (D>S); as a result, they are not easily obtained.

questions.q: Which is the highest bank in the banking system of India?
questions.explanation: As the Government’s banker and the bankers’ bank, the Reserve Bank of India (RBI) is the topmost bank in India’s banking system. The RBI, responsible for issuing currency notes and controlling monetary credit, was established on 1 April 1935 and was nationalised in 1949.

questions.q: Who amongst the following is the present Governor of the RBI?

options.E: None of the above/More than one of the above

questions.explanation: At the time of the question, the RBI Governor was Urjit Patel (September 2016 – December 2018). At present, the Governor of the Reserve Bank of India is Sanjay Malhotra (from December 2024). Before him, Shaktikanta Das was the Governor of the Reserve Bank of India.

questions.q: Which one of the following is not source of direct finance?

options.E: None of the above/More than one of the above

questions.explanation: All the institutions given in the options are sources of direct finance. However, NABARD does not provide direct finance to citizens, but it provides direct finance to food parks, cooperative banks, etc. Other institutions provide direct finance to citizens as well as to micro, small and large enterprises.

questions.q: Which of the following commercial banks of India come in the top 100 global banks?

options.E: None of the above / More than one of the above

questions.explanation: In April 2020, on the basis of total assets, India’s State Bank of India (SBI) ranked 55th among the world’s top 100 banks. As per the reports released in April 2025 and April 2024, SBI’s ranking was 43rd and 47th respectively. During the same period, HDFC Bank Ltd.’s ranking was 73rd and 74th respectively.

questions.q: Land Development Bank is a part of—
questions.explanation: “Land Development Bank” is the main institution of longterm cooperative credit Structure in the agricultural sector.

questions.q: Regional Rural Banks, also known as Gramin Banks, are classified as-

options.A: In the form of land development banks
options.B: In the form of branches of commercial banks

questions.explanation: Regional Rural Banks (RRBs) were established in 1975 with the objective of developing the rural economy—by providing credit and other facilities in rural areas for the development of agriculture, trade, commerce, industry and other productive activities, especially to small and marginal farmers, agricultural labourers, artisans and small entrepreneurs, and for related and incidental matters. Regional Rural Banks are classified under scheduled commercial banks.

questions.q: Note issue system in India is based on-
questions.explanation: Under the Reserve Bank of India (Amendment) Act, 1956, it was necessary to keep a minimum gold reserve of Rs. 115 crore and foreign securities worth Rs. 400 crore. However, under the Reserve Bank of India (Second Amendment) Act, 1957, the minimum combined reserve of gold and foreign securities was fixed at Rs. 200 crore, in which gold worth Rs. 115 crore was required and the remaining Rs. 85 crore was required in foreign securities.

questions.q: The Reserve Bank of India has decided to invest money to help in India's foreign trade-
questions.explanation: The Export-Import Bank of India (EXIM Bank), established in 1982, started its operations in March 1982. The objective of this bank is to provide financial facilities to exporters and importers. Along with this, it also provides refinance facilities to commercial banks and financial institutions for their export-import finance management activities. To meet its financial requirements, EXIM Bank can borrow from the Reserve Bank of India.

questions.q: According to the Reserve Bank of India, what is one of the eligibility criteria for a Small Finance Bank (SFB) to transition into a Universal Bank ?
questions.explanation: According to the Reserve Bank of India, with the objective of providing greater clarity, the eligibility criteria for SFBs to transition into a Universal Bank are as follows— 1. Scheduled bank status and a satisfactory track record of performance for a minimum period of five years. 2. The bank’s shares should be listed on a recognised stock exchange. 3. Minimum net worth of ₹1,000 crore at the end of the previous quarter (audited). 4. The prescribed CRAR requirements for SFBs must be met. 5. Net profit should have been earned in the last two financial years. 6. In the last two financial years, GNPA and NNPA should be less than or equal to 3% and 1% respectively.

questions.q: According to the UNDP Human Development Index (HDI) Report 2025, life expectancy in India increased from 58.6 years 6753 in 1990 to how many years in 2023?

options.D: More than one of the above

questions.explanation: According to the Human Development Report 2025 released by the United Nations Development Programme (UNDP), life expectancy at birth in India was 58.6 years in 1990, which increased to 72 years in 2023.

questions.q: Which of the following statements is not correct?

options.A: The Human Development Report is an annual publication officially released by the World Bank.
options.B: Life expectancy at birth measures the duration of life by age.
options.C: Adult literacy rate is used to measure knowledge.
options.D: Standard of living is measured by GDP Per Capita in US $ PPP, adjusted by purchasing power parity.

questions.explanation: The Human Development Report is published every year by the United Nations Development Programme (UNDP). It is released by considering three major dimensions of human development—per capita gross national income (in PPP terms), literacy rate, and life expectancy at birth—which correspond to a decent standard of living, knowledge, and a long and healthy life. The report was first published in 1990.

questions.q: Which of the following is not taken as one of the parts for preparing the “Human Development Index in India” under the United Nations Development Program (UNDP)?

options.A: Real GDP per capita income in US dollars

questions.explanation: The components used in constructing UNDP’s Human Development Index are— (i) Per capita Gross National Income (in dollars on the basis of purchasing power parity) (ii) Literacy rate (iii) Life expectancy at birth Therefore, except infant mortality rate, all the others are components of the Human Development Index (HDI).

questions.q: Human capital formation as a concept is better explained in terms of a process, which enables 1. individuals of a country to accumulate more capital 2. increasing the knowledge 3. increasing the skill levels 4. increasing the knowledge, skill levels and capacities of the people of the country Select the correct answer using the codes given below.
questions.explanation: Investment in education transforms humans into human capital. Thus, human capital represents increased productivity. It is an acquired ability and the result of well-considered investment decisions, made with the expectation of increasing future sources of income. Investment in education, workplace training, health, migration and information are sources of human capital formation.

questions.q: The Atmanirbhar Bharat Scheme announced by the Government helps in: (1) Enhancing India's manufacturing capabilities and exports across the industries (2) Incentivizing foreign investments for domestic production Out of these:
questions.explanation: The declared objective of Atmanirbhar Bharat Abhiyan is to increase domestic manufacturing capacity and develop India as a global supply chain and export hub. This campaign is not against foreign investment; rather, by liberalising the FDI policy in specific sectors, it encourages setting up production facilities in India itself (especially in defence and other manufacturing sectors).

questions.q: Consider the following statements regarding the SVAMITVA scheme : 1. It is a Central Sector Scheme under the Ministry of Mines. 2. This scheme seeks to create geo-positioning infrastructure like CORS network to benchmark the location and provides five centimetre level accuracy. 3. CORS means Cross-Origin Resource Sharing. 4. The scheme is a reformatory step towards establishment of clear ownership of property in rural inhabited (Abadi) areas, by mapping of land parcels using drone technology. Which of the above statements are incorrect?
questions.explanation: Started in April 2020, the full name of the SVAMITVA scheme is: SVAMITVA – Survey of Villages Abadi and Mapping with Improvised Technology in Village Areas. It is a Central Sector Scheme. The objective of this scheme is to provide an integrated property verification solution for rural India by using the latest drone survey technology to demarcate inhabited (abadi) land in rural areas. Under this scheme, there is a provision to establish the CORS (Continuously Operating Reference Stations) network, which is an important activity for accurate georeferencing, geoverification, and demarcation of land.

questions.q: Which one is not true about Ayushman Sahakar scheme?

options.A: The Finance Ministry of India launched this scheme
options.B: It is a scheme to assist cooperatives in the creation of health infrastructure
options.C: It specifically covers establishment, modernization, expansion, repairs, renovation of hospitals and healthcare and education infrastructure
options.D: It is formulated by the National Cooperative Development Corporation (NCDC)
options.E: None of the above / More than one of the above

questions.explanation: Launched on 19 October 2020, the Ayushman Sahakar Scheme is a scheme prepared by the National Cooperative Development Corporation (NCDC) under the Ministry of Agriculture and Farmers’ Welfare, Government of India. The objective of the scheme is to expand health facilities through cooperatives by setting up, repairing, and modernising healthcare and education infrastructure, hospitals, etc. At present, NCDC comes under the Ministry of Cooperation, Government of India.

questions.q: Choose the correct statement related to the National Pension System (NPS).

options.A: NPS is regulated by the Pension Fund Regulatory and Development Authority.
options.B: NPS is a retirement benefit scheme introduced by the Government of India to facilitate a regular income to all the citizens of India.
options.C: NPS is regulated by the IRDA.
options.D: NPS is regulated by the SEBI.
options.E: None of the above/More than one of the above

questions.explanation: The National Pension System (NPS) is mandatory only for Central Government employees. For State Government and other employees, it is not mandatory. It is regulated by the Pension Fund Regulatory and Development Authority (PFRDA). For all citizens of the country aged 18 to 70 years, it is a voluntary scheme. At present, the Central Government approved the Unified Pension Scheme (UPS) on 24 August 2024, which is effective from 1 April 2025.

questions.q: ‘Mission Indradhanush’, which was started in the year 2014, and the ‘Intensified Mission Indradhanush (IMI) 3.0’ scheme are related to which of the following?

options.C: Immunization of every child and every pregnant woman
options.E: None of the above/More than one of the above

questions.explanation: The Union Ministry of Health and Family Welfare launched the ‘Mission Indradhanush’ scheme in 2014. The objective of this mission is to immunize partially immunized and leftout children, as well as pregnant women. ‘Intensified Mission Indradhanush (IMI) 3.0’ was launched in February 2021. questions.explanation: Rupee convertibility means the free conversion of the rupee into foreign currencies and foreign currencies into rupees, without restrictions. Full convertibility of the rupee (on both the current account and the capital account) would mean no restriction on foreign capital entering or leaving India. As a result, adopting full convertibility would increase foreign investors’ confidence in the Indian economy and thereby raise inflows of foreign capital. Hence, achieving full convertibility of the Indian rupee is an important objective of India’s economic policy. It may be noted that since August 1994, the rupee has been fully convertible on the current account (on the trade account, it became partially convertible as early as March 1992). Regarding capital account convertibility, a committee was constituted in June 1997 under the chairmanship of S. S. Tarapore, which recommended a phased move towards capital account convertibility subject to certain conditions. Again, in March 2006, another committee (II) under S. S. Tarapore was formed to prepare a roadmap for capital account convertibility; after reviewing existing capital controls, it prepared a comprehensive, timebound five-year plan in three phases for capital convertibility. Although capital account convertibility does not exist at present, the Reserve Bank follows a highly liberal policy with respect to various capital transactions.

This foreign-currency basket included the currencies of five countries/groups—United States dollar, Japan’s yen, the United Kingdom’s pound sterling, China’s Renminbi (Yuan), and the euro. From March 1992 to March 1993, a dual system of a market rate and an administered (official) rate was adopted, and from March 1993 onward, the exchange rate of the rupee has been determined on the basis of demand and supply in the market.

questions.q: At present the country has adopted-

Under LERMS, 40% of foreign exchange earnings were converted at the exchange rate fixed by the Reserve Bank of India, and the remaining 60% at the market-determined rate. In 1993–94, the then Finance Minister Manmohan Singh declared the rupee fully convertible on the trade account (exports + imports). Moving further in this direction, in 1994–95 the rupee was made fully convertible on the current account of the balance of payments. At present, the rupee is fully convertible on the current account and partially convertible on the capital account.

questions.q: Which of the following is a cause of rural to urban migration in India ?
questions.explanation: Major reasons for migration from villages to cities in India include limited availability of employment in rural areas, higher demand for labour in cities, imbalanced development between villages and cities, availability of better opportunities for education, health, and employment in cities, and the attraction of urban infrastructure facilities and a better lifestyle. questions.q: Consider the following Statements : 1. Varsha Bima, the rainfall insurance scheme, is managed by the Agriculture Insurance Company of India Ltd. (AICIL). 2. The scheme was introduced during the 2007 South- West monsoon period. Which of the statements given above is/are correct?

In India, the Agriculture Insurance Company of India Limited is the designated institution to provide insurance cover to the agriculture sector. Earlier, the insurance schemes implemented in the agriculture sector were executed by the General Insurance Corporation of India (GIC); however, considering the extensive and specific requirements of the agriculture sector, the Government of India established the Agriculture Insurance Company of India Limited on 20 December 2002, which is the principal insurance institution responsible for providing insurance cover to the agriculture sector. The share capital of the Agriculture Insurance Company of India Limited includes investment by the General Insurance Corporation of India, National Insurance Company Limited, The New India Assurance Company Limited, Oriental Insurance Company Limited, United India Insurance Company Limited, and the National Bank for Agriculture and Rural Development (NABARD).

questions.q: Who was awarded the Nobel Prize in Economics in 1998?
questions.explanation: The Royal Swedish Academy of Sciences awarded Amartya Sen the Nobel Prize in Economics for the year 1998 for his significant contribution to welfare economics. According to the Academy’s citation, his contributions to welfare economics helped in understanding the economic mechanisms related to famine and poverty. Among the books written by Amartya Sen, “Collective Choice and Social Welfare”, “The Idea of Justice”, and “On Ethics and Economics” are the most discussed. The Nobel Prize in Economics for 2019 was given to Abhijit Banerjee, Esther Duflo, and Michael Kremer for their “experimental approach to alleviating global poverty”, whereas the Nobel Prize in Economics for 2022 was given to Ben S. Bernanke, Douglas W. Diamond, and Philip H. Dybvig. The Nobel Prize in Economics for 2023 was awarded to Claudia Goldin. The Nobel Prize in Economics for 2024 was awarded to three American economists—Daron Acemoglu, Simon Johnson, and James A. Robinson—for “studies of how institutions are formed and affect prosperity”. The Nobel Prize in Economics for 2025 has been jointly awarded to Joel Mokyr, Philippe Aghion, and Peter Howitt.

questions.explanation: The “Operation Blackboard” scheme started in 1987–88 to improve the human resources and physical facilities available in primary schools across the country. Providing two large classrooms, at least two teachers, and essential teaching-learning materials in every functioning school was the main feature of this scheme. As part of its expansion, in primary schools where enrolment was more than 100, provision was also made for a third teacher and a third classroom. From 1993–94, it was extended to upper primary schools as well. From 2002–03, this scheme was included in the Sarva Shiksha Abhiyan (Education for All Campaign).

questions.q: The principal foodgrain crops of Bihar are-
questions.explanation: The main foodgrain crops of Bihar are rice, wheat and maize.

questions.q: What form of agriculture is in Bihar? 1. Subsistence 2. Commercial 3. Export-intensive 4. Self-reliant Select your answer of the following codes–
questions.explanation: Bihar is a state with self-reliant agriculture.

questions.q: The area under agriculture in Bihar is –
questions.explanation: According to the Bihar Economic Survey, 2024–25, in 2022–23, 51.13 lakh hectares area (Net Sown Area) in Bihar is under agriculture.

questions.q: What is the crop density in Bihar?
questions.explanation: At the time of the question, option (a) was the correct answer. According to the Bihar Economic Survey, 2024–25, in 2022–23 the cropping intensity was 142%.

questions.q: In Bihar, tea gardens were established for the first time in which of the following places?

options.D: More than one of the above
options.E: None of the above

questions.explanation: In Bihar, tea gardens were established for the first time at Thakurganj (Kishanganj). It is noteworthy that tea is cultivated on about 25 thousand acres of land in Bihar. However, Kishanganj district is the principal place for tea cultivation in Bihar.

questions.q: The largest canal irrigated area of Bihar lies in the district of –

options.E: None of the above/More than one of the above

questions.explanation: In Bihar, in the matter of irrigation through canals, in 2020–21 Rohtas district ranked first with 3.07 lakh hectares; thereafter West Champaran (1.85 lakh hectares) and Aurangabad (1.61 lakh hectares) were next. In gross irrigated area also, Rohtas district ranked first with 4.15 lakh hectares. According to the Bihar Economic Survey, 2024–25, in 2022–23 the highest gross irrigated area through canals was in Rohtas district (299.40 thousand hectares). Thereafter, West Champaran (182.80 thousand hectares) was next.

questions.q: Which food industry dominates among the agro-based industries in Bihar?

options.D: More than one of the above
options.E: None of the above

questions.explanation: In Bihar, the two most important agro-based industries are food-grain–based industries and the sugar industry.

questions.q: At present, what is the main source of wealth of Bihar?
questions.explanation: At the time of the question as well as at present, agriculture remains the principal source of the state’s economy in Bihar.

questions.q: Which one of the following cereals has the highest per hectare yield in Bihar?

options.E: None of the above/More than one of the above

questions.explanation: According to data for the year 2018-19, the productivity (kg/ ha) of crops in Bihar was: Rice – 1948, Wheat – 2998, Maize – 4771 and Barley – 1990. Bihar Economic Survey, 2020-21 in the year 2019-20, productivity was: Rice – 2245 kg/ha, Wheat – 2595 kg/ha, Maize – 5193 kg/ha and Barley – 1369 kg/ha. Thus, maize recorded the highest productivity in both years. Bihar Economic Survey 2024-25 in the year 2023-24, productivity was: Rice – 3062 kg/ha, Wheat – 3211 kg/ha, Maize – 6138 kg/ha and Barley – 1641 kg/ha.

questions.q: What is the main crop of the Chotanagpur Plateau? (i) Rice (ii) Maize (iii) Pulses (iv) Wheat Choose your answer from the following codes-
questions.explanation: The main crops of the Chotanagpur Plateau are rice, wheat and maize. Among these crops, rice had the highest production.

questions.q: Which is the main cash crop of the state of Bihar?
questions.explanation: The major cash crops of Bihar are sugarcane, tobacco, jute and mesta. Among these, sugarcane occupies the first position in terms of both value and production.

questions.q: The top ranking pulses in terms of acreage in Bihar are –

options.E: None of the above/More than one of the above

questions.explanation: According to the Bihar Economic Survey 2019-20, in 2018-19, the production of Bhadai Moong was 5.32 thousand tons and that of Garma Moong was 113.16 thousand tons. Thus, the total Moong production was 118.48 thousand tons. During the same period, the production of lentils was 148.03 thousand tons, gram was 67.69 thousand tons, and Khesari was 51.38 thousand tons. Therefore, Moong and lentils held the top positions among pulses in Bihar. According to Bihar Economic Survey, 2024-25, in the year 2023-24, the production of lentils was 113.8 thousand tonnes, production of green gram was 117 thousand tonnes (Bhadai moong 4.6 + Garma moong 112.4 thousand tonnes), production of gram was 78.5 thousand tonnes and production of khesari was 33.1 thousand tonnes.

questions.q: What is the position of Bihar in terms of jute production among the states of India?

options.E: None of the above/More than one of the above

questions.explanation: At the time of the examination, the correct answer was option (c). At present, According to the Directorate of Jute Development Bihar ranks second in jute production in India, after West Bengal, while Assam occupies the third position.

questions.q: Which one of the following statements about irrigation in Bihar is not correct?

options.A: Of the total sown area in Bihar nearly 30 percent is irrigated.
options.B: Of the total irrigated area in Bihar nearly 30 percent is irrigated by canals and 39 percent by tubewells.
options.C: The maximum area irrigated by canals is found in Bhojpur, Aurangabad, West Champaran, Rohtas and Munger districts.
options.D: The maximum area irrigated by tube wells is found in Samastipur, Sitamarhi, Begusarai, Sitamarhi, Begusarai, Muzaffarpur, Gopalganj and Khagaria districts.

questions.explanation: At the time of the question, option (b) was the correct answer. According to the Bihar Economic Survey, 2024–25, in the year 2022–23, 78.39 percent of the gross cropped area of Bihar was irrigated. Of the total irrigated area of Bihar (5,697.9 thousand hectares), 30.28 percent area was irrigated by canals and 63.41 percent area by tube wells. The districts having the highest gross irrigated area through canals, respectively, are Rohtas, West Champaran, Bhojpur, Aurangabad and Kaimur. Whereas the districts having the highest gross irrigated area through tube wells, respectively, are Samastipur, Sitamarhi, Nalanda, Muzaffarpur and East Champaran.

questions.q: Joint irrigation project of the States of Bihar and Uttar Pradesh is –
questions.explanation: The Gandak Project is a joint project of Nepal and India. Through this project, the states of Bihar and Uttar Pradesh in India, as well as Nepal, are benefited. This project is constructed on the Gandak River near Valmiki Nagar in Bihar. Two canals have been taken out from it— (1) Tirhut Main Canal (2) Saran Main Canal

questions.q: From which of the following canal systems is irrigation done in the area of Bihar?

options.E: None of the above / More than one of the above

questions.explanation: According to the question, among the given options, irrigation in the area of Bihar is done by the Triveni Canal. This canal is related to the Gandak Irrigation Project. It is located in West Champaran district.

questions.q: Finally, what is the irrigation capacity of Bihar?
questions.explanation: At the time of the question, option (a) was correct. According to the Bihar Economic Survey, 2024–25, in the year 2023–24, the utilized irrigation potential of major and medium irrigation projects in Bihar was 26.7 lakh hectares, while the created irrigation potential was 37.72 lakh hectares. In the case of minor irrigation, the utilized potential was 43.31 lakh hectares, whereas the created potential was 48.12 lakh hectares.

questions.q: The traditional water conservation irrigation method prevalent in South Bihar is called -

options.E: None of the above/More than one of the above

questions.explanation: The traditional water conservation irrigation system prevalent in South Bihar is called Ahar–Pyne. In this system, retention ponds and channels or canals are used for the management of water resources.

questions.q: After independence the irrigated area in Bihar enlarged approximately-
questions.explanation: After independence, the irrigated area in Bihar has increased by approximately ten times. At present (2023–24), the created irrigation potential in Bihar is 85.84 lakh hectares.

questions.q: What type of banks are proposed to be set up in Bihar for agriculture and rural development?

options.E: None of the above/More than one of the above

questions.explanation: In October, 2021, during the 'Rabi Mahabhiyan' launched by the Chief Minister of Bihar, Nitish Kumar, it was announced to establish Krishi Yantra Bank for providing farmers with necessary agricultural implements for modern farming. Under this scheme, more than 100 agricultural machinery banks have been established in various districts of the state.

questions.q: Nepal's first transnational Petroleum Pipeline starts from which place in Bihar?

options.E: None of the above/More than one of the above

questions.explanation: Nepal’s first multinational petrol pipeline starts from Motihari in Bihar and goes up to Amlekhganj in Nepal. This 69 km. long pipeline was inaugurated on 10 September, 2019 by Nepal’s then Prime Minister K. P. Sharma Oli and India’s Prime Minister Narendra Modi.

questions.q: What was the power capacity availability in the Bihar state in the year 2019?

options.E: None of the above/More than one of the above

questions.explanation: At the time of the question, option (a) was the correct answer. As per the Bihar Economic Survey, 2024–25, according to the state’s generation plan, the estimated peak availability is 7157 MW in 2024–25 and 7463 MW in 2025–26.

questions.q: Per capita energy consumption of the state of Bihar is :

options.E: None of the above/More than one of the above

questions.explanation: In the context of the time of the question, option (a) was the correct answer. As per the Bihar Economic Survey, 2024–25, per capita electricity consumption in Bihar increased from 203 kWh in 2015 to 348 kWh in 2023. As per the provisional figures for 2024, per capita electricity consumption in Bihar has become 363 kWh.

questions.q: The latest annual per capita consumption of electricity in Bihar is –

options.E: None of the above/More than one of the above

questions.explanation: As per the Bihar Economic Survey, 2020–21, per capita electricity consumption in Bihar in 2019–20 was 332 kWh, which is the lowest level of electricity consumption in the country, whereas as per the Bihar Economic Survey, 2024–25, for 2024 (provisional), per capita electricity consumption in Bihar is 363 kWh.

questions.q: The three thermal power stations in Bihar run on coal are
questions.explanation: Bokaro, Chandrapura (Chandpura) and Santaldih are three coal-based thermal power stations. At present, Bokaro and Chandrapura are in the state of Jharkhand (earlier Bihar), while Santaldih is located in West Bengal. Therefore, both during the time of the question and even at present, Santaldih Thermal Power Station is located in the state of West Bengal. At present, in Bihar, coal-based thermal power stations such as Barauni, Barh and Kahalgaon are operated by NTPC.

questions.q: Kahalgaon, Kanti, Barh and Nabinagar are the centres for which of the following?

options.E: None of the above / More than one of the above

questions.explanation: Kahalgaon (Bhagalpur), Kanti (Muzaffarpur), Barh (Patna) and Nabinagar (Aurangabad) are centres of thermal power in Bihar.

questions.q: The Barh Super Thermal Power Station (BSTPS) is located in which state?

options.E: None of the above/More than one of the above

questions.explanation: Kahalgaon (Bhagalpur), Kanti (Muzaffarpur), Barh (Patna) and Nabinagar (Aurangabad) are centres of thermal power in Bihar.

questions.q: In which of the following years was the Bihar state Hydroelectric Power Corporation was established ?
questions.explanation: The Bihar State Hydroelectric Power Corporation (BHPC: Bihar State Hydroelectric Power Corporation) was established in 1982. It was an undertaking of the Government of Bihar. It worked for the development, installation, coordination, financing, and operation, etc. of all types of renewable energy projects in Bihar (such as hydroelectric, solar, wind, biomass, etc.).
